source.title: 4M: Massively Multimodal Masked Modeling
source.authors: David Mizrahi; Roman Bachmann; Oguzhan Fatih Kar; Teresa Yeo; Ming-Fei Gao; Afshin Dehghan; Amir Zamir

record.file_problem: not stated; the provided paper text appears complete.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports scaling results for a multimodal vision model and downstream validation losses, extending scale-related findings to a different modality and evaluation setting. It also varies architecture depth allocation and reports downstream losses.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit power laws. Its scaling tables report downstream transfer cross-entropy losses, not the pretraining-loss laws in V1–V3. It reports no fixed-compute optimal parameter/token allocation. The rows below concern downstream loss versus scale (V6) and architecture allocation (V4).
record.test_reason: 4M is a multimodal masked vision encoder-decoder. Kaplan et al. are cited only as motivation for Transformer scalability. Its 'scaling' ablations (Tables 21–23) report the best validation cross-entropy after fine-tuning on downstream token-prediction transfers. There are only four points per axis and no power-law fit, so the results cannot show power-law form (V1/V5), extrapolation (V2), compute-optimal allocation (V3) or fit-dependence (V7). V6 concerns language-model downstream performance, and V4 concerns language-model pretraining loss at fixed parameter count. The system here is a vision multimodal model and the measure is fine-tuned transfer loss, so these are related constructs, not tests. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude 4M scales with data, training length and model size on downstream transfer losses, and that encoder/decoder splits perform comparably, with balanced and encoder-heavy configurations slightly better. They also note that a 2.7B XL model overfit CC12M with limited downstream gain, so larger data or augmentation is needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses multimodal masked modeling for vision and assesses downstream transfer validation losses. It does not reproduce language-model held-out pretraining-loss scaling fits or compute-optimal allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream transfer performance varies with model size, pre-training duration, dataset fraction, and encoder/decoder depth allocation. The study also reports sensitivity to other training and masking choices, but those results do not test the claim versions recorded here.

fits_no_version.finding: In a multimodal masked vision model, the best fine-tuned validation cross-entropy averaged over transfers falls monotonically with scale, with no fit. By model size (24M–705M): 5.66, 5.51, 5.36, 5.23. By training tokens (50–400B): 5.46, 5.36, 5.29, 5.25. By CC12M fraction (1/64–1): 5.51, 5.44, 5.39, 5.36.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream transfer loss of multimodal masked vision models improves monotonically with model size, training tokens and data (no power-law fit).

fits_no_version.finding: Splitting 24 layers as 8/16, 12/12 or 16/8 between encoder and decoder gives average transfer loss of 5.38, 5.36 and 5.36. The reference average-loss std is 0.010.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Encoder/decoder depth split at fixed total depth matters little for downstream transfer loss in multimodal masked vision models.

record.problems: The reported scale results concern downstream transfer cross-entropy, not held-out pretraining loss; the study does not fit scaling laws or test prediction of larger runs. Dataset-size and architecture results are represented here only by average losses because of the row limit; the study reports separate task-category values as well. The preliminary 4M-XL run is described as overfitting to CC12M, with limited additional downstream improvement.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within the 60-row limit, retained all individual task-category and average-loss values for the model-size sweep (Table 23) and training-duration sweep (Table 22), but only average loss for dataset fractions (Table 21) and architecture depth allocation (Table 24). The omitted per-category values for Tables 21 and 24 are separate reported outcomes.

untested.parts: No pretraining held-out loss, no language model, no power-law fit.
No LM pretraining loss versus shape at fixed parameters; only one vision encoder/decoder split ablation on downstream loss.
Power-law form in the vision setting not fitted; only four points per axis on fine-tuned transfer loss.
No language-model downstream tasks; no predictive law or loss-to-downstream mapping.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

missing.what: Reference-model seed std devs (avg 0.010) and no-pretraining losses (avg 6.01), needed to judge whether scale differences exceed noise.
A 2.7B 4M-XL showed overfitting to CC12M and limited further downstream gain (no numbers).
Text-to-image FID falls with size: CC12M FID 15.9 (B), 11.9 (L), 10.7 (XL).

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan is cited only to motivate Transformer scalability. The 'scaling' here is a design ablation with four points per axis, measured on fine-tuned downstream token cross-entropy rather than pretraining loss, and with no fit. The reader's V4/V6 links were therefore dropped. The reader's 'supports' labels are not justified for language-model versions.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and orders of magnitude.
Whether fits on small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.

Width and other architecture changes; effects on held-out pretraining loss. The paper varies encoder/decoder depth allocation with total Transformer layers fixed at 24 and measures downstream transfer losses.
Whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
The study measures downstream validation cross-entropy against model size, training duration, and dataset fraction, but does not fit predictive laws or relate downstream results to pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The three tested encoder/decoder allocations with 24 total Transformer layers
reader_labels.reason: Average downstream loss is similar across the tested allocations, and the authors describe them as comparable; see A24-8-16, A24-12-12, and A24-16-8.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested 4M model sizes, 50B–400B training-token schedules, and CC12M dataset fractions
reader_labels.reason: Reported downstream validation losses generally decrease as model size, training duration, or dataset fraction increases; the rows measure downstream losses, not predictive-law accuracy.
